Answer: C
Reason: The combination of a reticulonodular pattern with cysts and nodules, specifically showing relative sparing of the costophrenic angles (medial tip of the right middle lobe/lung bases), is the classic radiological hallmark of Pulmonary Langerhans' cell histiocytosis. While the classifier suggests edema/opacity due to the diffuse nature of the disease, the specific morphological distribution described in the question and visible on CT (upper/mid-zone predominance with basal sparing) distinguishes PLCH from IPF (basal predominant) or LAM (diffuse cysts without nodules).
